You are working in the Ligra graph-processing framework at /workspace.
The framework (/workspace/ligra/*.h) is COMPLETE and already implements
vertexSubset, edgeMap/edgeMapData/edgeMapDense/edgeMapDenseForward/edgeMapSparse/
edgeMapSparse_no_filter, edgeMapFilter, packEdges, vertexMap, vertexFilter,
vertexFilter2 and parallel_main. DO NOT MODIFY ANY FILE under /workspace/ligra/,
and DO NOT MODIFY /workspace/apps/Makefile or any other app's .C file.
Your ONLY writable file is the single .C file named in your task.

Build & run (apps/ has symlinks to ../ligra/*.h already):
  cd /workspace/apps && make <AppName>
Compiler line: g++ -std=c++14 -O3 -DBYTERLE -o <App> <App>.C

CRITICAL framework facts (verify by reading the headers before coding):
* In the default build, parallel.h maps parallel_for -> plain `for` (single
  threaded). Code must still be written with correct atomics (CAS/writeMin/
  writeAdd) as upstream Ligra does, but execution is deterministic.
* Types: uintE/intE (32-bit by default), uintT/intT, UINT_E_MAX, INT_E_MAX.
* ligra/utils.h provides: CAS, writeMin, writeAdd, hashInt, newA, granular_for,
  sequence::plusReduce, sequence::plusScan, pbbs::* . There is NO writeOr --
  if you need atomic bitwise-or, define it locally in your .C file.
* edgeMap signature:
    edgeMap(graph<vertex>& GA, VS& vs, F f, intT threshold = -1, const flags& fl = 0)
  flags available: no_output, pack_edges, sparse_no_filter, dense_forward,
  dense_parallel, remove_duplicates, no_dense, edge_parallel.
  threshold -1 means "use GA.m/20".
* The user struct F passed to edgeMap must provide update(s,d),
  updateAtomic(s,d) and cond(d). For WEIGHTED apps the signatures are
  update(s,d,weight) / updateAtomic(s,d,weight).
* vertexMap(VS& V, F f) calls f(v) for a plain vertexSubset.
* vertexFilter(vertexSubset V, F filter) -> dense-based result.
  vertexFilter2(...) -> sparse-based result.
* vertexSubset constructors: vertexSubset(n) empty; vertexSubset(n, v) single
  vertex; vertexSubset(n, m, uintE* sparseArray); vertexSubset(n, m, bool* dense).
  Methods: isEmpty(), numNonzeros(), numRows(), toSparse(), toDense(), del(),
  vtx(i), isIn(v), dense().
* cond_true(d) is provided for "always true" cond functions.
* Every app is a template function:
    template <class vertex> void Compute(graph<vertex>& GA, commandLine P) {...}
  It MUST be a template over vertex, because parallel_main instantiates it for
  symmetricVertex, asymmetricVertex, compressedSymmetricVertex and
  compressedAsymmetricVertex. Therefore ONLY use the vertex methods that also
  exist on compressed vertices: getOutDegree(), getInDegree(),
  decodeOutNgh / decodeInNghBreakEarly / decodeOutNghSparse /
  decodeOutNghSparseSeq / countOutNgh / packOutNgh / copyOutNgh.
  *** DO NOT call getOutNeighbor(j) / getOutNeighbors() / getInNeighbor(j) in an
  app *** -- those do not exist on compressed vertices and the app must keep
  compiling once Ligra+ compressed vertices are implemented. If you need the
  neighbour list, materialize it with copyOutNgh (see apps/Triangle.C for the
  exact idiom) or use countOutNgh with a predicate.
* Read /workspace/apps/BFS.C, /workspace/apps/PageRank.C and
  /workspace/apps/Triangle.C first -- match their style, comment density and
  the 23-line MIT licence header they carry.
* /workspace/tutorial/*.C contains SKELETONS with "//FILL IN" markers showing
  the intended structure of some apps. Use them as structural hints only.

Inputs: ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100 (symmetric, unweighted, n=128 m=708,
run with -s) and ../inputs/rMatGraph_WJ_5_100 (symmetric, WEIGHTED, run with -s).

Always finish by actually building and running your app and confirming the
output is sane. Report exactly what you ran and what it printed.


You are an INDEPENDENT VERIFIER for /workspace/apps/PageRankDelta.C, which another agent just wrote.

The spec it was given was:
Implement /workspace/apps/PageRankDelta.C -- the delta-based (push) PageRank
variant from the Ligra paper. Read /workspace/apps/PageRank.C first: match its
constants and its reporting style.
* damping = 0.85, epsilon = 0.0000001, epsilon2 = 0.01,
  maxIters from P.getOptionLongValue("-maxiters",100).
* Arrays: double* p (accumulated rank), double* Delta, double* nghSum.
  p[i]=0, Delta[i]=1/n, nghSum[i]=0 initially.
* PR_F<vertex>(Delta,nghSum,V): update(s,d) adds Delta[s]/V[s].getOutDegree()
  into nghSum[d] and returns whether nghSum[d] was previously 0;
  updateAtomic does the same with a CAS loop; cond = cond_true.
* PR_Vertex_F_FirstRound (used only on round 1) sets
  Delta[i] = damping*nghSum[i] + (1-damping)/n, adds it into p[i], then
  subtracts the 1/n initialization from Delta[i], and returns
  fabs(Delta[i]) > epsilon2*p[i].
* PR_Vertex_F (later rounds) sets Delta[i] = damping*nghSum[i] and, when
  fabs(Delta[i]) > epsilon2*p[i], adds it into p[i] and returns 1.
* PR_Vertex_Reset zeroes nghSum.
* Each round: edgeMap(GA,Frontier,PR_F,GA.m/20, no_output | dense_forward),
  then vertexFilter over an all-vertices subset with the appropriate
  PR_Vertex_F to get the next frontier, then compute the L1 norm of Delta and
  stop when it is below epsilon, then reset nghSum.
* Report "PageRankDelta sum: <F>" (sum of p) and "PageRankDelta iters: <N>"
  with setprecision(10).
* The sum should be a sensible PageRank-like mass for this graph; compare it
  against ./PageRank -maxiters 100 -s -rounds 1 ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100
  and report both numbers.
* Run: ./PageRankDelta -maxiters 100 -s -rounds 1 ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100

Its report was:
**FILE WRITTEN:** `/workspace/apps/PageRankDelta.C` (only file created/modified; `/workspace/ligra/*` and `/workspace/apps/Makefile` untouched — their `M` status predates this task)

**COMMANDS RUN**
```
cd /workspace/apps && make PageRankDelta
  -> g++ -std=c++14 -O3   -DBYTERLE   -o PageRankDelta PageRankDelta.C
     (clean build, no warnings from PageRankDelta.C)

cd /workspace/apps && ./PageRankDelta -maxiters 100 -s -rounds 1 ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100
cd /workspace/apps && ./PageRank      -maxiters 100 -s -rounds 1 ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100
```

**FULL STDOUT — PageRankDelta**
```
PageRankDelta sum: 0.9751261894
PageRankDelta iters: 10
PageRankDelta sum: 0.9751261894
PageRankDelta iters: 10
Running time : 3.41e-05
```
(printed twice because `parallel_main` runs one warm-up round plus `-rounds 1`, exactly as `PageRank` does)

**FULL STDOUT — PageRank baseline**
```
PageRank sum: 0.980078125
PageRank sum: 0.980078125
Running time : 5.79e-05
```

**COMPARISON**
| app | sum | iters |
|---|---|---|
| PageRankDelta | 0.9751261894 | 10 (converged; L1(Delta) < 1e-7) |
| PageRank | 0.980078125 | ran to maxiters/convergence |

Both are just under 1.0 — the missing ~2% is rank mass absorbed by zero-out-degree vertices in this rMat graph, which neither variant redistributes. The 0.005 gap between the two is expected and inherent to the delta algorithm: `epsilon2 = 0.01` prunes vertices whose `|Delta| <= 0.01*p`, so those small residuals are never folded into `p`.

**CONVERGENCE SANITY CHECK** (`-maxiters k`, first line only)
```
k=1  -> sum 0.980078125    iters 1
k=2  -> sum 0.9800035625   iters 2
k=5  -> sum 0.9782673809   iters 5
k=20 -> sum 0.9751261894   iters 10   <- stops early, matches k=100
```
Monotone, and the iteration count saturates at 10 for any `maxiters >= 10`, confirming the L1-norm termination test fires rather than the iteration cap.

**IMPLEMENTATION NOTES**
- Constants, `newA`/`parallel_for` idiom, `setprecision(10)` reporting and the 23-line MIT header all mirror `PageRank.C`.
- `edgeMap(GA,Frontier,PR_F<vertex>(Delta,nghSum,GA.V),GA.m/20, no_output | dense_forward)` — I verified in `ligra/ligra.h:89` that `edgeMapDenseForward` dispatches through `decodeOutNgh`, which calls `f.updateAtomic` (`ligra/vertex.h:52`), so the CAS loop in `PR_F::updateAtomic` is the path actually taken.
- `nghSum` is reused as scratch for the `fabs(Delta[i])` L1 reduction and then zeroed by `PR_Vertex_Reset`, so no fourth array is allocated.
- Only `getOutDegree()` is used on vertices, so the app stays compilable against compressed vertices; no `getOutNeighbor`/`getOutNeighbors`.
- Compressed-vertex forward-compat and leak hygiene: `active.del()` is called on the early-break path before `break`, and `All`/`Frontier`/`p`/`Delta`/`nghSum` are all released at the end.

**CONCERNS**
- `-Wall` emits many `-Wreorder` warnings, but every one originates in `ligra/vertexSubset.h` (framework, not writable); none come from `PageRankDelta.C`.
- `PR_F::update`'s `oldVal == 0.0` return value is computed but discarded, since `no_output` means `edgeMap` ignores the update return. Kept because the task and upstream Ligra both specify that return semantics.
- Not tested under a parallel build (`CILK`/`OPENMP`) since the default `parallel.h` maps `parallel_for` to a serial `for`; the atomics are written correctly for the parallel case but were not exercised concurrently.

Your job: try to REFUTE that this app is correct and complete.
1. Read the file. Check it really implements the named algorithm (not a stub or a
   trivially-wrong shortcut), that it is `template <class vertex>`, and that it
   does NOT call getOutNeighbor/getOutNeighbors/getInNeighbor/getInNeighbors
   (those break on compressed vertices later).
2. Rebuild from scratch: cd /workspace/apps && rm -f PageRankDelta && make PageRankDelta
   -- it must compile with no errors. Warnings are acceptable.
3. Run it and check the printed numbers are actually right. Where feasible,
   compute the ground truth INDEPENDENTLY with a small python script over
   /workspace/inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100 (or rMatGraph_WJ_5_100 for the weighted
   app) and compare. Do not trust the implementation's own claims.
4. Confirm it does not modify anything under /workspace/ligra/, the Makefile,
   or another app (check: cd /workspace && git status --short).

If you find a real defect, FIX IT in PageRankDelta.C (that file only), rebuild,
rerun, and re-verify. Then report.

Return: VERDICT (PASS or FIXED or BROKEN), the ground-truth values you computed
independently, the values the app printed, and anything still wrong.

import sys
from math import fabs

# --- parse Ligra AdjacencyGraph ---
toks = open('/workspace/inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100').read().split()
assert toks[0] == 'AdjacencyGraph'
n = int(toks[1]); m = int(toks[2])
assert len(toks) - 1 == n + m + 2, (len(toks)-1, n+m+2)
offsets = [int(x) for x in toks[3:3+n]]
edges   = [int(x) for x in toks[3+n:3+n+m]]
deg = [ (offsets[i+1] if i < n-1 else m) - offsets[i] for i in range(n) ]
adj = [ edges[offsets[i]:offsets[i]+deg[i]] for i in range(n) ]
print("n=%d m=%d  zero-outdeg=%d  selfloops=%d" % (
    n, m, sum(1 for d in deg if d == 0),
    sum(1 for i in range(n) for j in adj[i] if j == i)))

maxIters = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 100
damping, epsilon, epsilon2 = 0.85, 0.0000001, 0.01
one_over_n = 1.0/n

p      = [0.0]*n
Delta  = [one_over_n]*n
nghSum = [0.0]*n
frontier = [True]*n

iters = 0
while iters < maxIters:
    iters += 1
    # (a) edgeMap: dense_forward -> for each i in frontier, push along out-edges,
    #     in vertex order, neighbour order (deterministic serial build)
    for i in range(n):
        if frontier[i]:
            di = deg[i]
            for ngh in adj[i]:
                nghSum[ngh] += Delta[i]/di
    # (b) vertexFilter over All
    nxt = [False]*n
    if iters == 1:
        addedConstant = (1-damping)*one_over_n
        for i in range(n):
            Delta[i] = damping*nghSum[i] + addedConstant
            p[i] += Delta[i]
            Delta[i] -= one_over_n
            nxt[i] = (fabs(Delta[i]) > epsilon2*p[i])
    else:
        for i in range(n):
            Delta[i] = nghSum[i]*damping
            if fabs(Delta[i]) > epsilon2*p[i]:
                p[i] += Delta[i]
                nxt[i] = True
            else:
                nxt[i] = False
    L1 = sum(fabs(d) for d in Delta)
    if L1 < epsilon:
        break
    nghSum = [0.0]*n
    frontier = nxt

print("PageRankDelta sum: %.10g" % sum(p))
print("PageRankDelta iters: %d" % iters)
print("  (L1 last = %.3e, frontier size after last filter = %d)" % (L1, sum(nxt)))

content.text:
VERDICT: **PASS** — no defect found, no changes made to `/workspace/apps/PageRankDelta.C`.

## Independent ground truth
I re-implemented delta-PageRank from the spec in Python (`/tmp/gt_prd.py`), parsing `/workspace/inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100` directly (n=128, m=708, 3 zero-out-degree vertices, 0 self-loops) and replicating the serial `dense_forward` push order exactly.

| `-maxiters` | Python ground truth (sum / iters) | App printed (sum / iters) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.980078125 / 1 | 0.980078125 / 1 |
| 2 | 0.9800035625 / 2 | 0.9800035625 / 2 |
| 3 | 0.97963691 / 3 | 0.97963691 / 3 |
| 5 | 0.9782673809 / 5 | 0.9782673809 / 5 |
| 9 | 0.9751261894 / 9 | 0.9751261894 / 9 |
| 10, 11, 20, 100 | 0.9751261894 / 10 | 0.9751261894 / 10 |

Exact agreement at all 10 printed digits, including the iteration count saturating at 10 (L1(Delta) reaches exactly 0.0 with an empty frontier, so the `L1_norm < epsilon` break fires, not the cap).

Two further independent cross-checks:
- **Closed-form total mass.** A separate power-method script converges to `0.980078125` in 75 iterations, matching `./PageRank`'s output. This is provably exact: the 3 zero-degree vertices are isolated, so each holds `0.15/128`, giving `total = 0.85*(total - 3*0.15/128) + 0.15` → `total = 0.980078125` exactly. So the PageRank baseline is right, and PageRankDelta's `0.9751261894` is a 0.5% under-count caused entirely by the specified `epsilon2 = 0.01` pruning (max per-vertex relative error vs the true fixed point: 2.6e-02 — consistent with epsilon2, not a bug).
- **Second graph.** A hand-built 4-vertex directed graph with no dangling vertices (`/tmp/tiny.adj`) gives `sum: 1` / `iters: 10` from both the app and Python, i.e. mass is exactly conserved when nothing leaks.

## Refutation attempts that failed to find anything
- **Not a stub / not a shortcut.** `/workspace/apps/PageRankDelta.C` is a faithful line-for-line match to upstream Ligra's PageRankDelta: `PR_F` with the double CAS loop, `PR_Vertex_F_FirstRound`, `PR_Vertex_F`, `PR_Vertex_Reset`, `edgeMap(...,GA.m/20, no_output | dense_forward)`, `vertexFilter` over an all-vertices subset, L1 norm via `nghSum` scratch, then `vertexMap(All, PR_Vertex_Reset)`.
- **Compare-before-vs-after-add.** `PR_Vertex_F` compares `fabs(Delta[i]) > epsilon2*p[i]` *before* `p[i] += Delta[i]`; `PR_Vertex_F_FirstRound` compares *after*. Both match the spec and upstream.
- **`-Wreorder` warnings do come from PageRankDelta.C** (lines 58-60, 75-77), not just the framework as the author claimed. But they are harmless: `addedConstant((1-_damping)*_one_over_n)` reads only constructor *parameters*, never the not-yet-initialized members. Proven empirically: `k=1` yields exactly `0.85*125/128 + 0.15`, which requires `damping` and `addedConstant` both correct. `PageRank.C` carries the identical idiom.
- **Compressed-vertex forward-compat.** No `getOutNeighbor`/`getOutNeighbors`/`getInNeighbor`/`getInNeighbors` anywhere; only `getOutDegree()`. `-Wall` output confirms `Compute` is actually instantiated for `symmetricVertex`, `asymmetricVertex`, `compressedSymmetricVertex` and `compressedAsymmetricVertex`, and all four compile.
- **Memory safety.** An `-fsanitize=address,undefined` build produced zero UBSan diagnostics and zero invalid reads/writes. LeakSanitizer reports only two framework leaks in `ligra/IO.h` (`stringToWords`/`readStringFromFile`, the commented-out `W.del()`), and one `alloc-dealloc-mismatch` in `graph<>::del()` at `ligra/graph.h:116`. **None** originate in PageRankDelta.C — its `p`/`Delta`/`nghSum`/`Frontier`/`All` are all released, and it `del()`s `active` on the early-break path (upstream actually leaks there).
- **Edge cases.** `-maxiters 0` → `sum: 0 / iters: 0`, no crash. Single isolated vertex → `sum: 0.15 / iters: 2`, which is hand-verifiable correct. `-rounds 3` gives identical results every round (state fully re-initialized). Running without `-s` (asymmetric instantiation) also gives `0.9751261894 / 10`, as expected since `dense_forward` and the sparse path both traverse out-edges.

## Commands run
```
cd /workspace/apps && rm -f PageRankDelta && make PageRankDelta
  -> g++ -std=c++14 -O3   -DBYTERLE   -o PageRankDelta PageRankDelta.C   (clean, no errors)
cd /workspace/apps && ./PageRankDelta -maxiters 100 -s -rounds 1 ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100
  -> PageRankDelta sum: 0.9751261894 / PageRankDelta iters: 10   (x2, then "Running time : 3.41e-05")
cd /workspace/apps && ./PageRank -maxiters 100 -s -rounds 1 ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100
  -> PageRank sum: 0.980078125   (x2, then "Running time")
plus: maxiters sweep {1,2,3,5,9,10,11,20,100}, -rounds 3, no--s run, /tmp/tiny.adj, /tmp/one.adj,
      -Wall build, -fsanitize=address,undefined build, python3 /tmp/gt_prd.py, /tmp/gt_pr.py, /tmp/cmp.py
```

## Scope check
`git status --short` on the protected paths shows only ` M apps/Makefile` and ` M ligra/ligra.h`, both of which were already `M` in the snapshot taken before this task began, plus untracked `ligra/byte*.h` from a concurrent Ligra+ agent. I made no edits to any file. The `apps/Makefile` `ALL=` line lists `BC` and `Components-Shortcut` alongside `PageRankDelta`, i.e. it was pre-populated with the full intended app set rather than appended to by this agent — and `make PageRankDelta` resolves through the generic `% : %.C $(COMMON)` rule regardless of `ALL`.

## Still-open items (not defects)
- `PR_F::update`'s `oldVal == 0.0` return value is unused under `no_output`. Correct per spec and upstream; dead but harmless. (Verified `decodeOutNgh` at `ligra/vertex.h:52` calls `updateAtomic`, so the CAS path is the one taken in the dense_forward case; the sparse path also uses `updateAtomic`. Both have identical semantics here.)
- Atomics were never exercised concurrently, since the default `parallel.h` maps `parallel_for` to a serial `for`. The CAS loop is written correctly for a parallel build but is untested under one.
